title: The Counter
goal: Increment the counter twice and get 2. One version compiles but counts a copy.
hints: Mutating a capture makes the closure FnMut - that's why bump itself is declared mut.
move on a Copy type doesn't move it. It copies it - and the closure bumps its private copy.
explanation: The borrowing closure mutably captures count: two bumps, count is 2, everyone's honest. The move version is the trap: i32 is Copy, so `move` captures a COPY - the closure diligently increments its own private counter while the function returns the untouched original. It compiles; it returns 0; only the test objects. (The two-argument closure just doesn't match the zero-argument calls - E0057.) Copy types + move closures deserve a second look every time.
